question: From which of the following countries were the principles of liberty, equality and fraternity taken in the Indian Constitution?
solution:
The correct answer is __**France**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **principles of liberty, equality, and fraternity** were taken from the French Revolution and were included in the Indian Constitution.
 
• **These ideals were integral to the democratic philosophy that influenced the Constitution, particularly in promoting individual freedoms and social justice.**
 
• These principles were central to the French motto "Liberté, égalité, fraternité", and they inspired the Indian leaders while drafting the Constitution.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **United Kingdom:**

 
 
• India’s constitutional framework was influenced by the British model, especially the parliamentary system and the rule of law.
 
• The concept of the Cabinet system, bicameral legislature, and law-making procedure were all drawn from the UK's political system.
 
• Parliamentary sovereignty and common law were also inherited.
 
 
 
• **Ireland:**
 
 
• The Directive Principles of State Policy in the Indian Constitution were inspired by the Irish Constitution.
 
• Ireland’s Constitution, which emphasized social welfare and justice, influenced India's approach to socio-economic rights.
 
 
 
• **United States of America:**
 
 
• The ideas of federalism and fundamental rights in the Indian Constitution were borrowed from the US Constitution.
 
• The system of judicial review, where courts have the power to examine and invalidate laws inconsistent with the Constitution, was another influence from the United States.
